title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is the continuation of La Longue Marche (1981), in the long section on 'tours de Lie' attached to a Teichmüller–Galois structure.

The objects:
- Pi: a profinite fundamental group.
- S (gothic) and M: a 'Teichmüller' (mapping-class-type) group and its arithmetic extension. M is roughly the Galois–Teichmüller group acting on the tower.
- Discrete versions pi_0, S_0 sit inside these.
- Pi, S, M underlined are 'algebraic envelopes', i.e. group schemes over Z (for M, only over Q).

On the previous page, Grothendieck assumes the component-group quotients are constant: underline-Gamma_X ≅ (Gamma_X)_{S_0}, with Gamma_X a finite quotient of X. These finite groups fit into the exact sequences (61). This lets him define groups Pi^Δ(Ẑ), S^Δ(Ẑ), M^Δ(Ẑ). These are, roughly, the Ẑ-points of the neutral component extended by the finite constant component group. They allow a 'profinite' comparison target even though Ẑ is not a field.

The maps (62) X → X^Δ(Ẑ) exist automatically for Pi and S, because pi_0 → Pi(Z) ⊂ Pi^Δ(Ẑ), and likewise for S_0. For M there is no discrete model, so the factorisation must be imposed as an axiom.

On this page Grothendieck does this over Q. Since M_Q/M_Q° is constant, one can define an adelic group M_Q^Δ(A_Q), presumably over the finite adeles. He then requires that the natural map M → M_Q(A_Q) factor through it; this is (63).

He then adds two strong optional axioms:
(i) the images of the three maps (62) are OPEN subgroups. He says this considerably strengthens a 'dividend/divisibility' condition from p. 749 (§40).
(ii) the composites X → X^Δ(Ẑ) → Gamma_X onto the finite component groups are surjective; this is (64).

When (i) and (ii) hold together with all previous conditions, he calls the setup a non-degenerate 'situation de Lie' over Z, called 'entière'. He crossed out 'développement' and 'parfaite'.

Purpose: to axiomatise when the profinite Teichmüller–Galois tower is 'controlled' by an algebraic group scheme over Z or Q. This is the algebraic/Lie-theoretic shadow of the tower. Openness of the image says the profinite group is, up to finite index, as large as the adelic or Ẑ-points of its algebraic envelope.

The next page shifts emphasis from pi_0 to a finite-index 'loop' subgroup pi_0'.
errors: No mathematical errors as such; this is a definitional sketch.
Defining X^Δ(Ẑ) via constant component groups over a non-field base needs care; it is not spelled out on this page.
The relation between the integral condition on M^Δ(Ẑ) in (62) and the adelic condition (63) over Q is left implicit.
The condition from p. 749 that openness 'strengthens' is illegible and is not stated here.

ideas.what: Algebraic group-scheme envelope (over Z, or over Q for the arithmetic part) of the profinite Teichmüller/Galois groups, with constant component group, used to define Ẑ-points and adelic points as comparison targets.
ideas.modern_name: Relative/weighted completion of mapping class groups and Galois groups; motivic Galois group of the Teichmüller tower
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (1989, P^1 minus 3 points); Hain, Hain–Matsumoto (relative and weighted completion, 1990s–2000s)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme alludes to 'Lie' aspects of the Teichmüller tower only vaguely; La Longue Marche (circulated) contains related material.

ideas.what: Requiring that the profinite group M map into the adelic points of its algebraic envelope M_Q(A_Q), factoring through M_Q^Δ(A_Q).
ideas.modern_name: Compatible system of l-adic representations into adelic points of an algebraic (motivic) group
ideas.usually_credited_to: Serre, Deligne; in this setting Hain–Matsumoto

ideas.what: Open-image axiom: the images of Pi, S and M in X^Δ(Ẑ) are open, together with surjectivity onto the component groups.
ideas.modern_name: Open image condition (Serre-type), analogous to Mumford–Tate/open image theorems; related to congruence-subgroup-type questions for mapping class groups
ideas.usually_credited_to: Serre (open image for elliptic curves); for Galois actions on fundamental groups: Ihara, Hain–Matsumoto (Zariski density results)

ideas.what: Terminology 'situation de Lie entière non dégénérée'.

missed.claim: Grothendieck formulates an axiom that the profinite Teichmüller–Galois groups have OPEN image in the Ẑ-points (and adelic points) of an integral algebraic group-scheme envelope with constant component group. He leaves open whether this holds for the actual Teichmüller tower.
missed.quote: Si de plus on suppose que les images des trois [lignes] (62) sont des sous-groupes ouverts ... on sera particulièrement heureux.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Hain–Matsumoto obtained Zariski-density/weighted-completion results for Galois actions on mapping class groups. An integral, open-image version over Ẑ is a stronger and less-studied question. For the mapping-class part it touches the congruence subgroup problem and the comparison between profinite completions and arithmetic envelopes.

missed.claim: Implicitly, the profinite Grothendieck–Teichmüller/Galois action is linked to an adelic integral 'Lie' structure. This is a Mumford–Tate/open-image paradigm for the whole Teichmüller tower, prefiguring motivic and weighted-completion approaches.
missed.quote: on exige que M → M_Q(A_Q) se factorise par (63) M → M_Q^Δ(A_Q)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is an early formulation of comparing the GT/Galois action with adelic points of a motivic group. Its integral (over Z) aspect is not standard in the later literature, which works mostly over Q or Q_l.

deep.surprise_reason: This is an unpublished axiomatisation of an integral/adelic 'Lie tower' with open-image conditions for the Teichmüller–Galois setup. It anticipates relative completion and motivic Galois group ideas. But it is a sketchy definitional page, and the general paradigm (algebraic envelopes, open image) is well known.
transcription_corrections: The superscript written as '^' / '\wedge' is a small triangle Δ in the image, consistent with the previous page: M_Q^Δ(A_Q), Π^Δ(Ẑ), 𝔖^Δ(Ẑ), M^Δ(Ẑ).
'des trois lieux [?] (62)' is more likely 'des trois lignes (62)'.
In (64) the target written 'Γ γ_Π' should be the component group \underline{Γ}_{\underline{Π}} (resp. for 𝔖 and M), as on the previous page.
In (64) the first source is probably Π (capital), not π.
'toutes les conditions sur [?] envisagées' is likely 'toutes les conditions supplémentaires envisagées'.
The word crossed out and replaced reads 'situation' (or similar) over a crossed-out 'développement'.
